title: evidence.nu: checkpoint grep pattern never matched run subjects
description:
Adopt from run 01M0NA4J5H30CZAFZEBF7HHQX5 (implementer checkpoint 23f073160).

Painpoint (planner@3 diagnosis): the checkpoint-base detection grepped for
'fabro.<run-id>:' but real checkpoint subjects are 'fabro(<run-id>):' —
zero matches, so the base fell back to HEAD and every evidence capture in
that run rendered empty diffs ('NO RUN BASE'). The reviewer correctly
rejected twice on missing evidence.

Fix (already on the product run branch): match the subject with
--fixed-strings on a derived subject mark instead of the broken pattern.
Port that evidence.nu into this branch's canonical copy under
.fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/.

Acceptance: .fabro/workflows/develop/scripts/evidence.nu uses the
fixed-strings subject match; nu-check passes; platform gate green.

title: qualitygate: go build must not recreate artifacts in the worktree
description:
Adopt from run 01M0NA4J5H30CZAFZEBF7HHQX5.

Painpoint: 'go build ./...' in the product qualitygate recreates the gofib
binary inside the worktree on every gate run, so the gate leaves the tree
dirty and reviewers flag artifacts the implementer never committed.

Fix (already on the product run branch): build into a temp directory
OUTSIDE the worktree (go build -o into an OS temp dir). On this platform
branch the canonical scripts/ tree holds only workflow tooling; this seed
exists so the convention is recorded platform-side: gates never write
build outputs into the worktree. Document the rule in the workflow's
implementer prompt if not already present.

Acceptance: no platform or product gate step writes artifacts into the
worktree; convention documented; platform gate green.

title: evidence: reorder sections so tail-truncation cannot hide the verdict-critical parts
description:
Adopt from run 01M0NA4J5H30CZAFZEBF7HHQX5.

Painpoint: the harness capture keeps only the tail of long command output
(~26 of 60 lines observed). evidence.nu printed the diff early and seed
specs last, so the 'NO RUN BASE' marker and tracker state were cut off and
the reviewer judged on a truncated tail.

Fix (already on the product run branch): order sections so the cheap,
verdict-critical parts come first — tracker state, in-progress seed specs,
changed-file stat, working tree — and the long diff last; keep sections
slim so typical captures fit. Port the reordering into this branch's
canonical copy.

Acceptance: evidence.nu emits tracker/spec sections before the diff;
nu-check passes; platform gate green.

title: Message bus: targeted message_send between stages (replaces last-writer-wins context relay)
description:
## Concept (from lab run 01M0QJ5FNE9 evidence)

Targeted messages between stages, NOT one shared context key that every
agent must faithfully restate.

## API

- Agent stages: tool `message_send(target, message)`
  - target: node id ('reviewer', 'planner', 'refiner', or a well-known
    mailbox like 'painpoints' / 'platform')
  - message: plain text (or JSON line) — bounded per message (e.g. 2KB)
  - the engine adds the SENDER stage id to the payload internally —
    provenance is structural, not claimed
- Deterministic stages (command nodes): a first-class command
  (`fabro message send ...` or nu script helper) with the same
  semantics — no LLM in the loop
- Delivery: messages addressed to stage X are injected into X's input
  (preamble section '## Messages' or equivalent) at X's next visit;
  messages to a mailbox are delivered by the refiner deterministically

## Why (three failures of the current relay, all observed)

1. TRUST: last-writer-wins requires each agent to restate the FULL
   accumulated list error-free; anything forgotten is silently deleted
   (fabro-meta-b3aa: planner claimed file writes that never happened)
2. GROWTH: the accumulated key grows per cycle (measured: 1.6KB -> 2.1KB
   in one run) — every cycle re-reads all history in every preamble,
   the exact accumulation the preamble budget exists to prevent
3. SABOTAGE: that growth pushed the 6.6KB evidence capture over the
   12KB aggregate budget, demoting it to a blobref the (tool-capable)
   reviewer was never told it could read — a full review cycle burned
   on delivery failure (run 01M0QJ5FNE9, reviewer painpoint)

## Design constraints

- messages are append-only per run; bounded per message; NOT context
  keys (no budget interaction, no restate requirement)
- sender provenance added by the engine, unforgeable by the agent
- persistence: same seam as checkpoints (durable across resume) —
  candidates: run event stream (already durable) + materialized file
  (.fabro/messages.jsonl) for agent pull
- reading side: addressed messages render into the target's prompt
  (## Messages section, after preamble scoping); pull access via a
  read tool can follow later (fabro-e804 family)
- supersedes the relay mechanics in fabro-176b (painpoint capture
  becomes message_send to the 'painpoints' mailbox; the refiner
  delivers from the message store, not from a context key)
- validation: lint unknown target node ids (warning, like
  preamble_stages_ignore)

## Open questions (design round needed)

- exact injection point (preamble section vs system message)
- per-mailbox message caps (unbounded painpoints mailbox = same growth
  problem one level up? likely: cap per sender per run)
- do parallel branches inherit the parent's messages?

## RESOLVED WITHOUT BUILDING (2026-08-23): hooks replace the bus

Grilled outcome: no message bus. The ONLY observed failure is the
N-writer painpoint accumulation; 1:1 handoffs over context keys work
correctly (last-writer-wins is RIGHT for 1:1). The StageComplete hook
(fabro-176b work item 2: extend HookContext with context_updates)
captures painpoints deterministically post-stage and routes them to the
mailbox — engine-added provenance for free (the hook knows node_id),
no restate relay, no new message store, no budget interaction.

Generalization if ever needed: targeted context keys (for.<node>.*)
rendered only at the target via existing scoping — not a bus.

Existing engine assets inventoried during this round (for any future
messaging work): SteeringHub (live human->agent, bounded queues),
Pairs (per-stage chat protocol, 8KB cap, idempotent, agent tool
access), node_outcomes provenance (structural, unexposed).
